title: FOMC communications blackout begins (through 2027-06-10)
source: EST: federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/files/fomc-blackout-period-calendar.pdf, re-downloaded 2026-09-05 (HTTP 200, 98,013 bytes) by this session. HONEST SOURCING NOTE: this session's content-stream inflation of that PDF recovered only document metadata, not the footnote text, so the policy rule below is quoted as INHERITED from two sibling ledgers that did extract it (fomc-2027-03-17 and fomc-blackout-start-2027-01-16), and only the arithmetic applied to it is this session's. The footnote states verbatim: 'The blackout period will begin at 12:00 a.m. Eastern Time the second Saturday before a meeting and end at 11:59 p.m. Eastern Time the day after a meeting. For example, if the Committee meeting starts on a Tuesday, the blackout period will begin at the start of the Saturday that falls ten days earlier, and if the meeting ends on a Wednesday, the blackout period will end at the end of Thursday.' Jun 8 2027 is a Tuesday and Jun 9 a Wednesday, so the source's own worked example gives Saturday 2027-05-29 through Thursday 2027-06-10 with no inference of ours. INDEPENDENTLY CONFIRMED without re-doing the work: fomc-2027-04-28's initial research decoded the same PDF's vector grid shading directly (fill-colour ops tracked, legend grey 0.851 = 'Blackout dates', validated first against the 2026 page) and returned all eight 2027 windows, the fourth of which is May 29 - Jun 10 — the Board's own highlighting, matching this arithmetic to the day. Filed estimate rather than confirmed because it is a firm rule applied to a TENTATIVE meeting date: fomccalendars.htm states every 2027 date is 'tentative until confirmed at the meeting immediately preceding it', so the promotion trigger is the 2027-04-27/28 meeting, not a better fetch. Discovered during the fomc-2027-06-09 initial research, checked 2026-09-05. AMENDED 2026-09-05 by this event's own initial research (docs/research/events/fomc-blackout-start-2027-05-29.md leg 1), which RETIRES the honest-sourcing caveat above: that session re-downloaded the same PDF (HTTP 200, 98,013 bytes), inflated 60 of its 122 content streams and recovered the footnote text VERBATIM rather than only metadata, so the policy rule is no longer inherited. It also DECODED the 2027 page's vector grid shading directly — 369 fill rectangles, of which 39 carry the legend's grey 0.851, against 365 day-number glyphs positioned by tracking the text and line matrices — and validated the decoder before believing it, by running it against the 2026 page, where it returns all eight known 2026 windows exactly (01-17→01-29, 03-07→03-19, 04-18→04-30, 06-06→06-18, 07-18→07-30, 09-05→09-17 which this calendar already carries as CONFIRMED, 10-17→10-29, 11-28→12-10). The 2027 page then returns 01-16→01-28, 03-06→03-18, 04-17→04-29, 05-29→06-10, 07-17→07-29, 09-04→09-16, 10-16→10-28, 11-27→12-09 — the fourth being this window, matching both the footnote arithmetic and fomc-2027-04-28's independent decode to the day. This is also the decode fomc-blackout-start-2027-03-06 attempted and disclosed as failed. The status stays estimate: the promotion trigger was never the fetch quality, it is the 2027-04-27/28 meeting
notes: The gate around the SECOND SEP of 2027 (fomc-2027-06-09, estimate), and its character comes from what sits at each end of the window rather than from what it covers. THE CLOSE IS THE FINDING: the gate lifts at the end of Thursday 2027-06-10, which is day one of the Bank of Japan's June MPM (boj-decision-2027-06-11, estimate) — so the first legal Fed voice after this decision lands on Friday 2027-06-11, the BoJ's own decision day. That is the June mirror of the asymmetry fomc-blackout-start-2027-03-06 measured for March, where the first Fed voice fell on triple witching, except the slot here is occupied by a central bank rather than an expiry. THE OPEN CROSSES A HOLIDAY: Memorial Day is Monday 2027-05-31 (nyse.com/markets/hours-calendars, fetched 2026-09-05, its own cell reads 'Monday, May 31'), so the window's first three days contain a single trading session. WHY THIS GATE IS UNUSUALLY EARLY: the fomc-2027-06-09 ledger's leg 2 measured that every 2027 FOMC sits exactly one day earlier than its 2026 counterpart EXCEPT June, which sits eight days earlier — the 2027 calendar is 2026's with one seven-day block moved out of the April-to-June interval and into June-to-July (2026 runs 49 42 49 42 days between decisions, 2027 runs 49 42 42 49). That makes 2027-06-09 the earliest June FOMC in the 21 years that ledger parsed, and it pulls this gate into May, which no recent June gate has done. The corridor it covers is nearly empty by the standards of the March window: the +/-5-day sweep around the decision returns exactly one tracked event (the BoJ), against five for March. Estimate widens caution only and licenses nothing; promote once the 2027-04-27/28 meeting confirms the 2027 calendar, and the date re-derives from whatever it confirms. AMENDED 2026-09-05 by this event's own initial research (docs/research/events/fomc-blackout-start-2027-05-29.md), which corrects two things this note asserted and adds the finding that displaced them. (1) 'THE CLOSE IS THE FINDING' IS DEMOTED: the close's coincidence with the BoJ stands, but the ledger's headline is the close's OTHER side. Measured from ^GSPC daily bars across 151 blackout windows 2007-2026 ex-2020, every window derived from the Board's own footnote rule applied to 166 parsed meetings, June's LAST IN-GATE session runs 1.145% mean absolute S&P move against a 0.693% June baseline and a 0.413% first post-gate session — 1.65x baseline and 2.77x the next session, the widest such ratio of the twelve months (January 0.72x, March 1.01x), larger in 13 of 18 years. That reverses fomc-blackout-start-2027-03-06's 'the gate boundary is not a volatility boundary' (0.64% vs 0.61%) and sharpens fomc-2027-06-09's 'June is the quietest month the Fed has' — reproduced exactly on decision days at 0.522% — to 'quietest ON THE DECISION DAY', since June is the only month whose day-after exceeds it by more than 2x (2.19x; next is October at 1.66x). So the named session is 2027-06-10, the gate's own last day, and 2027-06-11 is the pair it is tested against (registered FT-fomc-blackout-start-2027-05-29-1, score by 2027-06-14). (2) 'THE CORRIDOR IT COVERS IS NEARLY EMPTY' IS WRONG AS WRITTEN: it was measured on the DECISION's +/-5-day corridor, not on the gate's 8 trading sessions. BLS's own reference-week rule dates the MAY 2027 employment report to 2027-06-04 — inside this window, five sessions before the decision, with no official able to frame it — and the same derivation puts it inside the June gate in only 3 of 21 years (2020, 2024, 2027). Derived, NOT read: all four bls.gov schedule endpoints returned 403 to that session, so it is registered as FT-fomc-blackout-start-2027-05-29-2 rather than proposed as a calendar entry, the same line the March sibling drew. (3) THE MEMORIAL DAY FACT IS REFUSED ON MEASUREMENT, not amplified: this is the only 1 of 166 windows to contain Memorial Day, but a holiday inside a window is routine (MLK 16, Labor Day 5), an 8-session window is routine (33 of 155), and the deadline session runs 0.556% against a 0.698% May baseline — below (FT-fomc-blackout-start-2027-05-29-3). What the deadline DOES carry is an hour: SIFMA recommends a 2:00 p.m. ET fixed-income close on Friday 2027-05-28 (its 2027 US panel, fetched that session), so the operative Fed cutoff is 14:00 ET in the rates market where this chair's Fed risk lands, not the 16:00 equity close. Two entries proposed alongside: memorial-day-market-closure-2027-05-31 and sifma-bond-early-close-2027-05-28, both estimate.
